issue_142973.title: `platform` is missing from the tool-path hooks (pre_tool_call / post_tool_call / transform_tool_result)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

issue_142973.body:
### Summary

`pre_llm_call` receives `platform`; the tool-path hooks never do. A plugin that gates tool calls
therefore cannot distinguish an attended turn from an unattended one (`cron`, `subagent`,
`curator`) at the exact moment it has to decide whether to veto or only record.

### Where

All links are pinned to `81a55437f3`.

- [`agent/inline_tool_executors.py#L20`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/agent/inline_tool_executors.py#L20)
  — `tool_hook_ids()` builds the shared identity set (`task_id`, `session_id`, `tool_call_id`,
  `turn_id`, `api_request_id`) and never reads `agent.platform`, although `agent` is its first
  argument.
- [`hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1979`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1979)
  and [`#L1995`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1995)
  — the `pre_tool_call` payload is an explicit keyword list with no `platform`.
- [`model_tools.py#L643`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/model_tools.py#L643)
  — `_CallIds`, which backs `post_tool_call` and `transform_tool_result`, carries the same five
  fields.
- [`hermes_cli/hooks.py#L102`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/hooks.py#L102)
  — the `hermes hooks test` / `doctor` sample payloads mirror the runtime shape and lack it too.
- [`agent/turn_context.py#L819`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/agent/turn_context.py#L819)
  — by contrast, `pre_llm_call` passes it: `platform=getattr(agent, "platform", None) or ""`.

The hook catalog in `website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md` shows the same split: `pre_llm_call`,
`post_llm_call`, `transform_llm_output`, `pre_verify`, `pre_api_request`, `post_api_request` list
`platform`; `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `transform_tool_result` do not.

### Minimal reproduction — no turn needed

```python
from agent.inline_tool_executors import tool_hook_ids

class Agent:
    platform = "cron"
    session_id = "s"
    _current_turn_id = "t"
    _current_api_request_id = "a"

print(tool_hook_ids(Agent(), "task", "call"))
```

Actual:

```
{'task_id': 'task', 'session_id': 's', 'tool_call_id': 'call', 'turn_id': 't', 'api_request_id': 'a'}
```

Expected: the same dict plus `'platform': 'cron'`.

End to end the same thing is visible: register

```python
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", lambda **kw: print(sorted(kw)))
```

and let a cron job call any tool — `platform` is not in `kw`, even though the same run's
`pre_llm_call` gets it.

### Why it matters

I maintain `provenance-gate` (in the plugin catalog via #141935), which refuses a "decision-shaped"
write unless it can point at a quote the user actually typed in this session. In an attended turn
that is the right default. In a cron run there
is no user message to quote, so every such write would be refused while nobody is watching — the
gate has to run in observe mode there. Without `platform` in the hook the plugin cannot make that
distinction, so it stays in observe mode everywhere, i.e. the check cannot be enabled by default
for anyone. The workaround available today is guessing from `session_id` prefixes or lock files,
which is not something a policy hook should do.

### Scope

The whole class, not just `pre_tool_call`: the same identity set backs `post_tool_call` and
`transform_tool_result`, and tool-side middleware receives the same kwargs, while LLM-side
middleware already gets `platform` (`agent/turn_api_request.py`), so the two sides disagree today.
Shell hooks receive identity fields in `extra` (`agent/shell_hooks.py#L87`), so they pick the fix
up without any extra code.

### Environment

`main` @ `81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa`, Windows 11, Python 3.14.7.
I have a patch ready and will open the PR right after this issue.

issue.body:
### What

`pre_llm_call` has always carried `platform`; `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call` and
`transform_tool_result` never did. This threads `agent.platform` through the shared identity set so
a policy hook can tell an attended turn from an unattended one (`cron` / `subagent` / `curator`).

Fixes #142973.

### Why the shared set, not three call sites

`tool_hook_ids()` is the single place that builds the identity kwargs for the tool path, and
`_CallIds` is the single carrier for the two `model_tools` paths. Adding the field there means the
three hooks, tool-side middleware and the inline executors all agree, and no future hook call site
can forget it.

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `agent/inline_tool_executors.py` | `tool_hook_ids()` adds `platform` (and its docstring says why) |
| `model_tools.py` | `_CallIds.platform`; `_emit_post_tool_call_hook(platform=...)`; `handle_function_call(platform=...)` |
| `hermes_cli/plugins.py` | `_get_pre_tool_call_directive_details(platform=...)` forwards it to the `pre_tool_call` payload |
| `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` | `_pre_tool_block_message()` now reuses `tool_hook_ids()` instead of re-listing the ids; the registry dispatch passes `platform` |
| `agent/tool_executor.py` | registry dispatch passes `platform` |
| `hermes_cli/hooks.py` | `_DEFAULT_PAYLOADS` sample payloads gain `"platform": "cli"` (used by `hermes hooks test` / `doctor`) |
| `website/docs/.../hooks.md` + `zh-Hans` mirror | catalog rows and the `pre_tool_call` parameter table document `platform` |
| `tests/agent/test_tool_hook_platform.py` | 6 unit invariants (all red on the base) |
| `tests/cron/test_cron_tool_hook_platform.py` | end-to-end: real scheduler tick, real plugin load, `platform == "cron"` |

### Coverage — every construction site accounted for

| Identity source | Carries `platform` |
|---|---|
| `tool_hook_ids()` (all 7 call sites: `agent_runtime_helpers` ×2, `inline_tool_executors` ×2, `tool_executor` ×3) | yes, single source |
| `_CallIds` (3 constructions: `model_tools` ×2, +1 via `tool_hook_ids`) | yes |
| `post_tool_call` emit (`_emit` → `asdict(ids)`) | yes |
| `transform_tool_result` emit (`ids.hook_kwargs()`) | yes |
| `pre_tool_call` emit (`**ids.hook_kwargs()` / `**tool_hook_ids(...)`) | yes |
| tool request/execution middleware (`**hook_kwargs`) | yes |

### Notes reviewers may want

- **Middleware alignment, not a side effect.** Tool-side middleware signatures are
  `**context`, and LLM-side middleware already receives `platform`
  (`agent/turn_api_request.py`). Both sides now see the same field.
- **Shell hooks get it for free.** `_payload_fields()` promotes only `tool_name` / `args` /
  `session_id` / `parent_session_id`; everything else lands in `extra`, so `platform` shows up in a
  shell hook's JSON without any shell-specific change. Covered by a test.
- **Callers with no agent keep today's behaviour.** The code kernel, MCP bridge, TUI/connector
  dispatch call `handle_function_call()` without `platform`; the field defaults to `None` and the
  wire value is `""`, exactly as the other identity fields behave outside a turn.
- **Additive keyword field**, which is the pattern `plugins/AGENTS.md` prescribes: callbacks are
  signature-inspected, so narrow signatures are unaffected and `**kwargs` callbacks get the field.
- **Append-only signature growth.** `platform` is the *last* parameter of `handle_function_call`
  and of `_CallIds`, so no existing positional call changes meaning — the repo convention of adding
  keyword fields without reshaping the existing ones holds even for the semi-public entry point.

### Tests

`scripts/run_tests.sh` could not bootstrap on my machine (its pinned `uv` download is blocked), so
I ran its own per-file runner directly with the same env (`TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8 PYTHONHASHSEED=0`):

```
before (base 81a55437f3):  2 files, 0 passed, 7 failed
after  (this branch):      2 files, 7 passed, 0 failed
```

Related suites (re-run on this branch): `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py`,
`tests/hermes_cli/test_hooks_cli.py`, `tests/agent/test_shell_hooks.py`,
`tests/cron/test_cron_execution_identity.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_hook_failure_reporting.py`
→ `144 passed, 1 failed, 12 skipped` (`151 passed / 1 failed / 12 skipped` including the two new
files); the one failure
(`TestPluginDiscovery::test_enabled_portable_plugin_registers_components`) also fails on
`81a55437f3` on Windows (portable-plugin `app.darwin.location` validation), i.e. pre-existing and
unrelated.

`python scripts/check` → `12 checks, ok`.

### Docs

Catalog table (three rows) + the `pre_tool_call` parameter table, in `website/docs` and the
`zh-Hans` mirror.

### Disclosure

Drafted with an AI assistant under my direction; I reviewed the diff and ran the checks above.

+"""Tool-path hooks carry ``platform`` — the same value ``pre_llm_call`` already gets.
+
+Contract under test: a plugin that gates tool calls can tell an attended turn from an
+unattended one (``cron`` / ``subagent`` / ``curator``) without guessing from session ids.
+Covers all three tool hooks (pre/post/transform) plus the shell-hook ``extra`` dict.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from agent.inline_tool_executors import tool_hook_ids
+from model_tools import _CallIds, _apply_transform_tool_result_hook, _emit_post_tool_call_hook
+
+
+def _agent(platform="cron"):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        platform=platform,
+        session_id="sess-1",
+        _current_turn_id="turn-1",
+        _current_api_request_id="api-1",
+    )
+
+
+def test_tool_hook_ids_carries_agent_platform():
+    ids = tool_hook_ids(_agent("cron"), "task-1", "call-1")
+    assert ids["platform"] == "cron"
+    # Unknown platform (older agent object, programmatic caller) coerces to "" like the other ids.
+    assert tool_hook_ids(SimpleNamespace(), "t", "c")["platform"] == ""
+
+
+def test_call_ids_round_trips_platform_into_hook_kwargs():
+    ids = _CallIds(**tool_hook_ids(_agent("subagent"), "task-1", "call-1"))
+    assert ids.hook_kwargs()["platform"] == "subagent"
+
+
+def test_pre_tool_call_hook_receives_platform(monkeypatch):
+    from hermes_cli import lifecycle
+    from hermes_cli.plugins import _dispatch_pre_tool_call_hooks
+
+    seen = {}
+

commit.message:
feat(hooks): pass platform to the tool-path hooks

pre_llm_call has carried `platform` all along; pre_tool_call, post_tool_call and
transform_tool_result never did. A policy plugin therefore cannot tell an attended
turn from an unattended one (cron / subagent / curator) at tool time, which is
exactly where a gate has to decide whether to veto or only record.

Thread `agent.platform` through the shared identity set instead of per-call-site
plumbing: tool_hook_ids() adds the field, _CallIds carries it into the two
model_tools paths, and the directive helper forwards it. `hermes hooks test` /
`doctor` sample payloads gain the field too, and the hook catalog documents it in
both locales.

Observable effects beyond the three hooks: shell hooks receive it in `extra`,
and tool-side middleware now sees the same `platform` the LLM-side middleware
already gets (agent/turn_api_request.py), so the two sides agree.

Callers without an agent (code kernel, MCP bridge, TUI/connector dispatch) pass
nothing and keep the empty string, i.e. today's behaviour.

Tests: tests/agent/test_tool_hook_platform.py (unit, all red on the base),
tests/cron/test_cron_tool_hook_platform.py (real scheduler tick + real plugin
load; asserts platform == "cron").

turn from an unattended one (cron / subagent / curator) at tool time, which is
exactly where a gate has to decide whether to veto or only record.

Thread `agent.platform` through the shared identity set instead of per-call-site
plumbing: tool_hook_ids() adds the field, _CallIds carries it into the two
model_tools paths, and the directive helper forwards it. `hermes hooks test` /
`doctor` sample payloads gain the field too, and the hook catalog documents it in
both locales.

Observable effects beyond the three hooks: shell hooks receive it in `extra`,
and tool-side middleware now sees the same `platform` the LLM-side middleware
already gets (agent/turn_api_request.py), so the two sides agree.

Callers without an agent (code kernel, MCP bridge, TUI/connector dispatch) pass
nothing and keep the empty string, i.e. today's behaviour.

Tests: tests/agent/test_tool_hook_platform.py (unit, all red on the base),
tests/cron/test_cron_tool_hook_platform.py (real scheduler tick + real plugin
load; asserts platform == "cron").

labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
### Summary

`pre_llm_call` receives `platform`; the tool-path hooks never do. A plugin that gates tool calls
therefore cannot distinguish an attended turn from an unattended one (`cron`, `subagent`,
`curator`) at the exact moment it has to decide whether to veto or only record.

### Where

All links are pinned to `81a55437f3`.

- [`agent/inline_tool_executors.py#L20`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/agent/inline_tool_executors.py#L20)
  — `tool_hook_ids()` builds the shared identity set (`task_id`, `session_id`, `tool_call_id`,
  `turn_id`, `api_request_id`) and never reads `agent.platform`, although `agent` is its first
  argument.
- [`hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1979`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1979)
  and [`#L1995`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/plugins.py#L1995)
  — the `pre_tool_call` payload is an explicit keyword list with no `platform`.
- [`model_tools.py#L643`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/model_tools.py#L643)
  — `_CallIds`, which backs `post_tool_call` and `transform_tool_result`, carries the same five
  fields.
- [`hermes_cli/hooks.py#L102`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/hermes_cli/hooks.py#L102)
  — the `hermes hooks test` / `doctor` sample payloads mirror the runtime shape and lack it too.
- [`agent/turn_context.py#L819`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa/agent/turn_context.py#L819)
  — by contrast, `pre_llm_call` passes it: `platform=getattr(agent, "platform", None) or ""`.

The hook catalog in `website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md` shows the same split: `pre_llm_call`,
`post_llm_call`, `transform_llm_output`, `pre_verify`, `pre_api_request`, `post_api_request` list
`platform`; `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `transform_tool_result` do not.

### Minimal reproduction — no turn needed

```python
from agent.inline_tool_executors import tool_hook_ids

class Agent:
    platform = "cron"
    session_id = "s"
    _current_turn_id = "t"
    _current_api_request_id = "a"

print(tool_hook_ids(Agent(), "task", "call"))
```

Actual:

```
{'task_id': 'task', 'session_id': 's', 'tool_call_id': 'call', 'turn_id': 't', 'api_request_id': 'a'}
```

Expected: the same dict plus `'platform': 'cron'`.

End to end the same thing is visible: register

```python
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", lambda **kw: print(sorted(kw)))
```

and let a cron job call any tool — `platform` is not in `kw`, even though the same run's
`pre_llm_call` gets it.

### Why it matters

I maintain `provenance-gate` (in the plugin catalog via #141935), which refuses a "decision-shaped"
write unless it can point at a quote the user actually typed in this session. In an attended turn
that is the right default. In a cron run there
is no user message to quote, so every such write would be refused while nobody is watching — the
gate has to run in observe mode there. Without `platform` in the hook the plugin cannot make that
distinction, so it stays in observe mode everywhere, i.e. the check cannot be enabled by default
for anyone. The workaround available today is guessing from `session_id` prefixes or lock files,
which is not something a policy hook should do.

### Scope

The whole class, not just `pre_tool_call`: the same identity set backs `post_tool_call` and
`transform_tool_result`, and tool-side middleware receives the same kwargs, while LLM-side
middleware already gets `platform` (`agent/turn_api_request.py`), so the two sides disagree today.
Shell hooks receive identity fields in `extra` (`agent/shell_hooks.py#L87`), so they pick the fix
up without any extra code.

### Environment

`main` @ `81a55437f31a9f12a30c53b6c5d49d420898aa`, Windows 11, Python 3.14.7.
I have a patch ready and will open the PR right after this issue.
